document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Rep Won't Seek UN Seat For Now
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] US officials meet a Taliban representative who says the Taliban want US influence rather than Iranian, Pakistani or Russian. The source describes three internal Taliban factions and extensive Pakistani/ISI support: cash, supplies, military/intelligence advisers and even drafting letters.

events.description: Two-hour call by a Taliban representative on A/S Raphel with Coldren and Chew present
Planned UNOCHA aid conference in Ashgabat
Najibullah taken from UN compound and executed
Taliban representative made a two-hour call on A/S Raphel, with Coldren and Chew present.
Planned UNOCHA aid conference in Ashgabat, mid-January; India and Russia to attend.
State cable reporting Taliban rep won't seek UN seat for now.
Raphel met with an Afghan interlocutor and discussed Taliban broadening, Pakistani support, and the King's return; reported in cable.
State Department comment that it had received more credible information about the extent and origin of Pakistani assistance to the Taliban.

relationships.quote: PAKISTANI SUPPORT RANGED FROM CASH TO SUPPLIES TO LOGISTICAL SUPPORT TO ON THE GROUND MILITARY/INTEL ADVISERS

relationships.detail: ISI described as an element of the Government of Pakistan.
relationships.quote: STRONG TIES EITHER TO GOP ELEMENTS SUCH AS ISI OR TO PAKISTAN'S RELIGIOUS PARTIES

relationships.detail: Taliban members educated in Pakistani religious schools have strong ties to religious parties.

relationships.quote: TOOK FORMER PRESIDENT NAJIBULLAH TO AN UNDISCLOSED LOCATION AND EXECUTED HIM

relationships.detail: Rabbani decided the corpse should be hung in the street.
relationships.quote: MULLAH RABBANI WHO DECIDED THAT THE CORPSE SHOULD BE HUNG IN THE STREET

relationships.quote: KHALOIS WERE THE ONES WHO STORMED THE UN COMPOUND

relationships.detail: Taliban administration in Kabul.
relationships.quote: BRING THEM INTO THE TALIBAN ADMINISTRATION IN KABUL AND ELSEWHERE

relationships.detail: Raphel said the US would underscore the need to broaden the Taliban in its ongoing dialogue with Taliban officials.
relationships.quote: RAPHEL SAID THAT WE WOULD UNDERSCORE THAT POINT IN OUR ONGOING DIALOGUE WITH TALIBAN OFFICIALS.

relationships.detail: Despite the Taliban getting Pakistani backing, the source saw them as intrinsically Afghan.
relationships.quote: DESPITE THE FACT THAT THEY GET PAKISTANI BACKING, HE NEVERTHELESS SAW THE TALIBAN AS INTRINSICALLY AFGHAN

relationships.detail: ISI officers and recruits operate as Pakistani 'soldiers' in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: TWO SORTS OF PAKISTANI "SOLDIERS" IN AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: Raphel said the US could not give the King financial support or a US imprimatur, but he should return and test the waters.
relationships.quote: IT WAS NOT POSSIBLE TO GIVE THE KING FINANCIAL SUPPORT OR A U.S. IMPRIMATUR.

relationships.detail: It was suggested the King could go to Mazar-i-Sharif as a first destination to reassure non-Pashtuns.
relationships.quote: HE COULD GO TO A NON-PASHTUN AREA LIKE MAZAR-I-SHARIF.

relationships.detail: Zahir Shah fears Iran might prevent his return.
relationships.quote: ZAHIR SHAH ALSO FEARS THAT IRAN MIGHT TRY TO PREVENT HIS RETURN.

relationships.detail: Raphel offered to explain US policy to Gen. Abdul Wali should he visit the US.
relationships.quote: RAPHEL SAID SHE WOULD BE HAPPY TO EXPLAIN USG POLICY TO GEN. ABDUL WALI SHOULD HE DECIDE TO VISIT THE U.S.

relationships.detail: Abdul Wali is associated with the King as his representative.
relationships.quote: WE WILL SEE THE KING'S REPRESENTATIVES.

relationships.detail: Message signed by Christopher, Secretary of State.
relationships.quote: CHRISTOPHER

sources_cited: Taliban representative's account to A/S Raphel (name redacted)
key_claims: The Taliban representative said Pakistani support, largely via ISI, ranged from cash and supplies to on-the-ground military and intelligence advisers.
Taliban policy is influenced most by madrasa-educated members with ties to ISI and Pakistani religious parties, rather than veteran mujahideen fighters.
About 100 former Khalqi officers inside the Taliban were said to be anti-US and responsible for harassment of foreigners and Najibullah's killing.
The Taliban claimed to control two-thirds of Afghanistan and could not be assumed to go away.
The US declined to provide funding or backing to any Afghan faction, including the King.
